V. Validation for insurance claim

The validation of an insurance claim ensures that it aligns with the baseline established during the initial project assessment. The insured must initiate the claim, after which the insurer appoints a qualified validator to review it. This process may include an on-site inspection to verify the claim's legitimacy. The key steps in the validation process are as follows:
\- Review of claim and past reports: the validator examines the claim alongside previous validation reports, including design, implementation and annual assessments.
\- On-site inspection and documentation: if required, the validator conducts a walkthrough audit to assess the current condition of the project or equipment.
\- Energy savings verification: the reported energy savings are compared against the committed values, referencing implementation and annual validation reports.
\- Compliance assessment and decision: any deviations from the contract terms are identified and the claim is either approved or rejected based on the agreement set during implementation.
\- Investigation of performance issues: if energy savings do not meet expectations, the validator determines the underlying cause and may initiate a separate inquiry if needed.
The following documents are mandatory for the insurance validation process:
\- Project design validation report and associated documents
\- Project implementation validation report and associated documents
• Legal and valid contract between the insurer and the insured party
• Annual validation report and associated documents (if applicable)

The validator has the sole authority to approve or reject the claim based on a valid assessment report. However, if the insured disputes the decision, they may challenge it on merit, as per the arbitration clause outlined in the contract between the insurer and the insured. Normally, the standardised contract stipulates that the opinion of the validation entity should be accepted by the parties so that the decision of the arbitration is not questioned.

To enhance the understanding of key stakeholders in India, a business case is prepared for a forging MSME cluster near New Delhi. The forging industry in India is a vital pillar of the country's manufacturing ecosystem, significantly supporting key sectors such as automotive, power and general engineering. The forging sector faces persistent challenges such as volatile steel and industrial fuel prices, rising input costs and increasing competition from imported components - particularly from China, Japan, Korea and Europe. Forging operations typically involve energy-intensive processes such as furnace heating, hammering and machining, powered by fossil fuels and electricity. Additionally, many units employ heat treatment furnaces and compressed air systems, further increasing energy demand. With appropriate technology upgrades and efficiency interventions, the sector can achieve significant energy savings, making it more sustainable and cost-effective.

\- The first initiative focuses on replacing traditional furnaces with energy-efficient models, which generally provide superior insulation, enhanced combustion control and improved thermal efficiency. Such upgrades can lead to substantial reductions in fuel consumption and minimised heat losses, resulting in both lower operational costs and reduced emissions. This process of replacing the furnace can save up to 25% of energy (as per the published data of EE furnaces).

\- The second project involves switching from conventional fossil fuel-powered furnaces to induction furnaces. Induction furnaces use electricity and offer precise temperature control, faster heating cycles and a cleaner process without direct combustion emissions. These furnaces provide an environmentally friendly alternative that aligns well with modern forging operations and can save up to 15-20% energy in the process.

\- The third project aims at upgrading to IE3 (Premium Efficiency) motors, replacing standard motors. These high-efficiency motors operate at a significantly better energy performance level compared to older or less efficient counterparts, reducing electrical energy use, enhancing system reliability, and lowering operating temperatures. This improvement not only cuts energy costs but also extends equipment life and reduces the frequency of maintenance and can provide energy savings of up to 20%.

Together, these three projects promise considerable energy and cost savings while also presenting scalable, replicable solutions that can be adopted by small and medium-sized forging enterprises. The specific savings potential in each case may slightly vary, depending on the chosen technology, operating conditions and possible interactions with other energy efficiency measures that are being implemented. Implementing these initiatives would lead to enhanced productivity, a reduced environmental footprint and contribute positively to India's broader goals of energy security and sustainable development.

7 Next steps
The following steps will be taken to support the rollout of the ESI scheme in India:
\- The BEE will launch the ESI Implementation Roadmap in alignment with the ADEETIE scheme in 2026 to operationalise the ESI scheme.

\- The BEE will convene a Technical Committee (TC) comprised by main actors for the implementation of the ESI scheme to coordinate implementation activities and ensure alignment with the ADEETIE scheme. The TC should then convene regular meetings under the chairmanship of the DG-BEE.
\- The design and implementation of ESI pilot projects, and the creation of a pipeline of projects could be coordinated by the TC with guidance from the BEE.

\- The BEE, supported by the facilitating entity and other partners, should (i) identify capacity building needs of key stakeholders and define targeted training programmes, and (ii) develop standardised templates, contracts and other documents.
\- Based on the learnings from an initial rollout of both the ESI scheme and the ADEETIE scheme, the BEE could develop a long-term strategy for embedding the ESI scheme in phase II of ADEETIE.

Annex B. International case studies
This annex provides a review of selected international case studies on ESI and EEI. They include:

A. Energy savings insurance
Eight case studies on the implementation of the energy savings insurance in Colombia, Chile, Morocco and Mongolia are presented below.
Energy savings insurance for SMEs in Colombia

With the support of the Inter-American Development Bank, and in collaboration with BANCOLDEX, Colombia has become the first country in Latin America and the Caribbean to issue energy saving policies under the Energy Savings Insurance Program (ESI) to the benefit of small and medium-sized enterprises that have invested in energy efficiency and power generation projects.
Case study A1: Hospital Méderi
Location: Colombia
Programme: Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program
Partners: Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), BANCOLDEX

Background: Hospital Méderi, the largest hospital network in Colombia, recognised the need to address its growing demand for reliable hot water across its Bogotá facility. To modernise and put in place a more sustainable solution, the hospital embarked on a project to install a new thermal system. With the support of the ESI programme, the institution aimed to find a trusted technology provider and achieve the desired outcomes (IDB, 2019[24]).
Project description:

\- Technology implemented: the project at Hospital Méderi involved the installation of 220 solar collectors on the hospital's rooftops to guarantee a continuous supply of hot water and fulfil the 24/7 needs of hot water in the patient rooms and other hospital areas.
\- Total investment: USD 200 000 was allocated for the complete overhaul, installation and integration of the new system.
ENERGY SAVINGS INSURANCE IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP OF INDIA © OECD 2026

\- Energy source transition: the replacement led to a drastic reduction in the consumption of natural gas, transitioning a majority of the hot water heating load to a cleaner and more sustainable source (BASE, 2024[25]).
Achieved benefits:
\- Annual energy savings: The hospital achieved guaranteed energy savings of approximately USD 23 000, leading to a payback period of nine years (BASE, 2024[25]).

\- Operational efficiency: The new heating solution provided a reliable and consistent hot water supply, improving the comfort and service quality for students, staff and faculty. It also reduced maintenance demands and enhanced system longevity.
Impact:

\- Support for SMEs and green tech providers: The project fostered collaboration with local SMEs offering energy-efficient technologies and installation services, further promoting green economic development.

\- Replication potential: The success of this initiative underlined the replicability of energy efficiency projects backed by insurance mechanisms, making it easier for other institutions to follow suit with confidence in their return on investment (IDB, 2019[24]).
Case study A2: Villa Martha Hotel
Location: Colombia
Programme: Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program
Partners: Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), BANCOLDEX

Background: The Villa Martha Hotel, a boutique hospitality business in Colombia, recognised the rising cost of electricity and the environmental impact of its energy consumption. As part of its commitment to sustainability, guest comfort and cost-efficiency, the hotel sought to integrate renewable energy into its operations.

Hospitality businesses, especially smaller, family-run establishments like Villa Martha, often face financial and technical barriers when investing in clean energy. The ESI Program, supported by the IDB and BANCOLDEX, provided the hotel with the tools and security to confidently invest in solar energy by offering technical validation and performance guarantees (IDB, 2019[24]).
Project description:
\- Technology implemented: the hotel installed a 10 kilowatt-peak (kWp) photovoltaic (solar PV) system, designed to offset a significant portion of the hotel's electricity demand.
• System specifications:
\- Rooftop-mounted photovoltaic panels
On-grid configuration with net metering to feed surplus power back into the local electricity grid (BASE, 2024[25]).
\- Total investment: USD 30 000, covering system design, equipment procurement, installation and technical validation (IDB, 2019[24])
Achieved benefits:
Electricity cost reduction: the PV system significantly reduced the hotel's reliance on grid electricity, cutting energy bills and protecting the business from future tariff increases.
ENERGY SAVINGS INSURANCE IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP OF INDIA © OECD 2026
\- Energy independence: the solar system improved energy resilience, especially important in regions susceptible to grid instability.

\- Insurance-backed performance: through the ESI Program, the Villa Martha Hotel was able to secure performance insurance, ensuring that the expected energy savings from the solar system would be met or losses compensated. This drastically reduced investment risk and was a key enabler for project financing (BASE, 2024[25]).
Impact:

\- Tourism and sustainability alignment: the Villa Martha Hotel positioned itself as a sustainable tourism destination, appealing to eco-conscious travellers and strengthening its market differentiation.
\- SME empowerment: the project demonstrates how small businesses can harness renewable energy with the right financial and risk-mitigation tools in place.

\- Scalability: The success of this project shows that even small-scale installations, when supported by the right mechanisms, can make a meaningful impact on both operational costs and environmental performance (BASE, 2024[25]).
Case study A3: Neiva Plaza Hotel
Location: Neiva, Colombia
Programme: Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program
Partners: Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), BANCOLDEX.

Background: the Neiva Plaza Hotel, a well-established business in the heart of Neiva, faced rising operational costs due to its aging and inefficient boiler-based water heating system. The existing method was reliant on a 24-year-old pyro-tubular boiler that was fuelled by liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). The system was generating nearly 6 000 hot water litres per day for laundry, kitchen and showers, resulting in high levels of pollution and operating costs (IDB, 2019[24]). Through Colombia's Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program, the hotel found the ideal platform to confidently invest in new clean energy technology with guaranteed performance outcomes.
Project description:
\- Technology implemented: the hotel replaced its old fossil-fuel boilers with a solar thermal water heating system, a clean and efficient technology suitable for hotels with high hot water demand.

\- System capacity: the project consisted of replacing the old boiler with 22 solar collectors installed on an area of 61.7 m2 with five backup heat pumps, resulting in the reduction of gas consumption by 70%. With each collector producing between 10 000 and 12 000 British thermal units (BTU) per hour, the hotel achieved efficient heat production for a 6 000-litre tank, maintaining a temperature range of 50 to 55 degrees Celsius (BASE, 2024[25]).
\- Total investment: USD 25 000 was invested in the project, covering equipment, installation, and engineering services (IDB, 2019[24]).
Achieved benefits:
\- Energy savings: The new solar thermal system achieved an impressive 70% reduction in energy consumption compared to the previous boiler setup. This translated into major utility cost savings.
ENERGY SAVINGS INSURANCE IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP OF INDIA © OECD 2026
\- Cost savings: The investment of USD 25 000 yielded guaranteed energy savings of approximately USD 8 000 per year.

\- Simple payback period: Thanks to high energy savings and relatively low investment, the project's simple payback period was less than 3 years, making it a highly attractive financial decision (BASE, 2024[25]).
Strategic impact:

\- Sustainability commitment: the Neiva Plaza Hotel elevated its reputation as an environmentally responsible business in the tourism sector, aligning with growing guest expectations for green hospitality practices.
\- Cost control and profitability: the reduced energy costs directly contributed to improved profitability and allowed the hotel to reinvest savings into other service areas.
Case study A4: Agrícola El Retorno S.A. - Chile
Location: Chile
Programme: Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program
Sector: Agriculture
Partner: Inter-American Development Bank (IDB)

Background: Agrícola El Retorno S.A., a farming enterprise in Chile, was facing increasing energy expenses due to its high reliance on grid electricity for daily operations. In pursuit of long-term sustainability and cost stability, the company decided to invest in clean energy. Through the Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program, the company accessed performance-guaranteed technology, risk mitigation, and financing mechanisms to install a solar energy system on its premises.
Project description:
\- Technology implemented: installation of an on-site solar photovoltaic (PV) system to generate clean electricity for agricultural operations.
\- Capacity: 63 kW of capacity designed to meet a significant portion of the farm's daytime energy demand.
\- Total investment: USD 134 328 covering the design, purchase and installation of the solar PV system (Netto et al., 2020[26]).
Achieved benefits:
\- Annual energy savings: the system produces approximately 107 600 kWh per year, reducing dependency on grid electricity.
\- Annual cost savings: estimated at USD 11 768 per year, contributing to long-term operational cost reductions.
\- Simple payback period: approximately 12 years, after which the company continues to benefit from nearly free solar power (Netto et al., 2020[26]).
\- Energy resilience and independence: the solar system offers greater control over energy costs and supports business continuity during power outages or price spikes.
Impact:
ENERGY SAVINGS INSURANCE IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP OF INDIA © OECD 2026
\- Sustainable agriculture leadership: Agrícola El Retorno's project positions the company as a leader in sustainable farming, demonstrating how clean energy can be integrated into agriculture.
\- Boost for the clean tech market: the initiative supported local technology providers and installers, enhancing growth in Chile's distributed solar energy sector.

\- Model for replication: With its straightforward implementation and measurable returns, this solar PV project stands out as a replicable model for other SMEs in the agricultural sector across Latin America (Netto et al., 2020[26]).
Case study A5: Ariztía El Paico poultry processing plant
Location: El Paico, Chile
Programme: Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program
Sector: Food processing/poultry industry
Partner: Inter-American Development Bank (IDB)

Background: Ariztía, a leading poultry processing company in Chile, sought to enhance energy efficiency at its El Paico processing plant, one of its most energy-intensive facilities. With rising electricity costs and growing environmental commitments, the company turned to the Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program to support a high-impact industrial upgrade, focused on replacing aging electric motors with newer, high-efficiency models.
Project description:
\- Technology implemented: replacement of three large-capacity electric motors to improve process efficiency and reduce electricity consumption.
• Motor capacities: 600 kW, 522 kW and 336 kW
\- Total investment: USD 80 279 for procurement, installation, and commissioning of the energy-efficient motors (Netto et al., 2020[26]).
Achieved Benefits:
\- Annual energy savings: the new motors deliver energy savings of 43 319 kWh per year, reducing the plant's electricity footprint.
\- Annual cost savings: the plant benefits from approximately USD 46 223 in cost savings annually, significantly improving its operating margins.
\- Simple Payback Period: Less than 2 years, making it a financially attractive investment with rapid returns (Netto et al., 2020[26]).
\- Improved Operational Reliability: The upgraded motors reduce downtime and maintenance costs, enhancing overall production efficiency.
Impact
\- Industrial energy efficiency showcase: Ariztía's motor replacement project serves as a prime example of how industrial process upgrades can yield rapid financial and environmental returns.
\- Risk reduction via ESI: the ESI mechanism mitigated performance risk, giving Ariztía confidence in the expected savings and enabling a smooth financing process.
ENERGY SAVINGS INSURANCE IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP OF INDIA © OECD 2026

\- Inspiration for sector-wide adoption: the project sets a precedent for energy efficiency improvements in Chile's broader food processing sector, encouraging similar investments across the industry (Netto et al., 2020[26]).
Case study A6: Bayas del Sur S.A.
Location: Chile
Programme: Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program
Sector: Food processing/agroindustry
Partner: Inter-American Development Bank (IDB)

Background: Bayas del Sur S.A., a prominent company in the Chilean agro-industrial sector known for processing berries and other fruit-based products, was seeking to modernise its production infrastructure. The company identified its aging steam boiler as a major source of energy inefficiency and operational cost. To reduce fuel consumption and lower emissions, Bayas del Sur engaged with the Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program to de-risk investment in a new, energy-efficient boiler system.
Project description:
\- Technology Implemented: installation of a new energy-efficient industrial boiler to replace an older, less efficient system.
\- Capacity: 3 tons of steam, sufficient to meet the plant's process heating demands more efficiently.
\- Total Investment: USD 230 100, covering the full equipment upgrade and installation (Netto et al., 2020[26]).
Achieved benefits:
\- Annual energy savings: the new boiler generates approximately 665 000 kWh in energy savings per year, significantly reducing fuel consumption.
\- Annual cost savings: the company now saves an estimated USD 39 000 per year on energy costs, contributing directly to operational profitability.
\- Simple payback period: less than 6 years, after which the investment continues to generate annual savings and operational efficiencies (Netto et al., 2020[26]).
\- Improved environmental performance: the modern boiler emits fewer pollutants and supports the company's sustainability goals.
Impact:
\- Advancement in sustainable agroindustry: this project highlights the role of energy-efficient technologies in enhancing competitiveness and sustainability in the agro-processing sector.
\- Risk mitigation through ESI: The use of energy savings insurance gave Bayas del Sur confidence in the projected benefits, enabling the company to secure financing with reduced risk.

\- Scalable success for industrial applications: the successful outcome of this project positions it as a scalable model for similar facilities in Chile and the wider Latin American region looking to upgrade core energy systems (Netto et al., 2020[26]).

Case study A7: Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Programme - Morocco
Country: Morocco
Programme: ESI Programme
Partners: BASE (Basel Agency for Sustainable Energy), Moroccan Agency for Energy Efficiency (AMEE), local financial institutions
Target audience: Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) across priority sectors

Background: In Morocco, SMEs form the backbone of the economy, yet they often face significant barriers when it comes to adopting energy-efficient technologies. These include limited technical know-how, financing challenges and perceived investment risks. To address these barriers and promote sustainable development, Morocco launched the Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Program, an innovative initiative designed to de-risk energy efficiency investments.

Led by BASE in collaboration with AMEE and local financial institutions, the ESI Program empowers Moroccan SMEs to transition toward cleaner, more efficient operations while also boosting confidence among investors and insurers through standardised procedures and guaranteed performance.
Project scope and technologies:
The Moroccan ESI Program supports a wide range of energy-efficient technologies, including:
• High-efficiency lighting systems
• Industrial and commercial motors
• Compressed air systems
\- Boilers and heat recovery systems
• Refrigeration units
• Heating and air conditioning (HVAC)
• Solar panels for electricity generation
• Solar water heaters for thermal applications
Financial impact:
\- Initial investment: approximately USD 31 million invested in energy efficiency projects during the first three years of implementation
• Total accumulated investment: reached USD 141 million by the end of six years
\- Energy savings achieved: estimated total energy savings of 1 450 GWh over a 15-year operational period - equivalent to the annual consumption of thousands of households

\- Cost Savings: While exact monetary savings are not disclosed, the energy savings imply substantial operational cost reductions and improved financial resilience for participating SMEs (BASE, 2022[27]).
Key implementation strategies:
The program strategically concentrated on high-energy-consumption sectors, such as:
• Industry (e.g. food processing, textiles, chemicals)
• Commercial buildings (e.g. hotels, retail, office complexes)
• Agriculture (e.g. irrigation systems, cold storage)
Impact:
ENERGY SAVINGS INSURANCE IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP OF INDIA © OECD 2026
\- Scalable model: Morocco's experience showed that ESI can be successfully scaled when combined with strong institutional partnerships and local market engagement.
\- Market development: by lowering perceived risk and increasing technical capacity, the program stimulated a new market for energy efficiency solutions tailored to SMEs.

\- Financial innovation: the use of insurance as a risk-mitigation tool enabled greater access to financing from local banks and investors, even for SMEs with limited collateral or credit history (BASE, 2022[27]).
Case study A8: ESI Programme - Mongolia
Location: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
Programme: Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) Programme
Partners: BASE (Basel Agency for Sustainable Energy), Tenger Insurance, Monhorus

Background: Located in Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia - one of the world's most polluted and coldest capital cities - XacBank recognized the urgent need to address its growing energy demands and environmental impact. The bank's headquarters, which houses an energy-intensive server room, consumed significant amounts of electricity annually. In line with its corporate sustainability goals, XacBank became the first institution in Mongolia to pilot the Energy Savings Insurance (ESI) model, aiming to reduce operational costs and greenhouse gas emissions through the implementation of a renewable energy solution.
Project description:

\- Technology implemented: The project involved the installation of a rooftop photovoltaic (solar PV) system with a total capacity of 19.62 kW. The system was specifically designed for optimal solar exposure on the bank's central office building and to support critical energy loads such as the server infrastructure.

\- Energy source transition: by shifting a portion of its energy use from the grid to solar power, XacBank decreased its dependence on conventional electricity sources, contributing to Mongolia's broader efforts to adopt cleaner, low-emission energy technologies.
\- Total investment: an investment of approximately USD 33 000 was made to cover system design, installation and integration into the building's energy supply (BASE, 2024[25]).
Achieved benefits:
\- Annual energy generation: the solar PV system generates approximately 22 000 kWh per year, covering about $20\%$ of the building's total electricity needs.

\- Cost savings and efficiency: by generating its own clean energy, the bank achieved considerable long-term savings on electricity costs while reducing operational risks associated with energy price volatility (BASE, 2024[25]).

\- Performance assurance: with support from the Energy Savings Insurance, provided by Tenger Insurance, the bank was assured of the system's energy output - reducing investment risk and strengthening internal confidence in the project's returns.
Impact:

\- Sustainability leadership: XacBank demonstrated corporate leadership in environmental sustainability, becoming the first organisation in Mongolia to implement the ESI model and setting a benchmark for similar institutions in the region.
ENERGY SAVINGS INSURANCE IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP OF INDIA © OECD 2026
\- Support for the local green economy: the project engaged local providers, such as Monhorus for installation and engineering services, fostering the growth of Mongolia's green technology sector.

\- Replication potential: following the project's success, a second ESI-backed solar project was announced in December 2023 for an E-Mart supermarket, with a 32-kW capacity system expected to generate 80 000 kWh annually. This highlights the replicability of the model across sectors (BASE, 2024[25]).
B. Energy efficiency insurance
Five case studies are presented below on the application of the energy efficiency insurance in the United Kingdom (UK) and United States of America (USA).
Case study B1: Energy efficiency insurance in a 5-Star hotel - United Kingdom
Location: United Kingdom
Programme: HSB Energy Efficiency Insurance (Munich Re)
Partners: Munich Re/HSB

Background: an independent 5-star hotel in the UK, built in 1996 and comprising 174 rooms, faced high operational costs due to inefficient energy use, with an annual energy spend of approximately USD 4 million. In an effort to modernise its systems, reduce emissions and improve profitability, the hotel committed to a multi-technology energy efficiency retrofit. Leveraging the HSB Energy Efficiency Insurance solution provided by Munich Re, the hotel was able to access financial protection for both performance and operational risks.
Project description:
• Technology implemented: A total of seven energy-saving initiatives, including:
• Combined Heat and Power (CHP) plant
• LED lighting installation
• Building Management System (BMS) upgrade
• Variable Speed Drives (VSDs)
• Rooftop solar PV panels
\- Upgrades to air conditioning and extraction systems
• Building Type: Independent 5-star hotel (174 rooms)
• Total Investment (CapEx): USD 3,500,000 (HSB UK and Ireland, 2026[28])
Achieved benefits:
\- Estimated annual energy savings: approximately USD 575 000 per year, reducing the hotel's energy intensity and operational costs.
\- Annual revenue from energy initiatives: around USD 375 000, showcasing clear commercial gains.
• Insurance coverage:
○ Material damage and breakdown: USD 3 500 000
○ Loss of revenue: USD 375 000

Insured energy savings: USD 575 000 (over a 5-year term) (HSB UK and Ireland, 2026[28])
Insurance solution: The HSB Energy Efficiency Insurance offered by Munich Re provided a comprehensive risk mitigation framework, including:
\- Coverage for equipment breakdown, material damage and underperformance of energy-saving systems
• Protection against shortfalls in guaranteed savings
• Support for business interruption losses related to energy systems
Impact:

\- De-risked investment: The insurance made it easier for the hotel to secure project financing, giving confidence to lenders and investors by protecting against technical and financial uncertainties.
\- Sector-specific application: demonstrated how customised insurance packages for hospitality can unlock large-scale energy efficiency upgrades.
\- Financial and environmental payoff: the project showcases the synergy of technical solutions and financial instruments, combining infrastructure improvement with guaranteed returns.
Case study B2: Munich Re's Performance Guarantee Insurance for Xicato's LED modules
Client: Xicato, a U.S.-based LED lighting company
Partner: Munich Re

Traditional LED warranties only cover failures or workmanship defects for one year. Customers, especially in retail and hospitality, demanded stronger assurances on long-term performance, specifically colour consistency and brightness.
Solution:
Xicato introduced a 5-year performance guarantee on its LED modules:
• Color stability: Minimal deviation over time.
• Lumen maintenance: Minimum 70% light output after five years.
\- Munich Re underwrote this guarantee, a portion of the financial risk after auditing Xicato's development and manufacturing processes (Programbusiness.com, 2013[29]).
Industry significance:
This coverage complements Munich Re's portfolio of performance guarantees for renewable technologies, advancing insurance's role in accelerating adoption of sustainable innovations.
Impact:
\- First of its kind: pioneering insurance-backed LED performance guarantee.
• Xicato reduced long-term risk exposure on its balance sheet, freeing capital for growth.
• Provided independent validation and boosted buyer confidence.
Key learnings:
\- Insurance-backed guarantees reassure customers about long-term LED performance (colour stability, brightness).
ENERGY SAVINGS INSURANCE IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP OF INDIA © OECD 2026
\- Risk transfer to Munich Re helped Xicato reduce financial liability and invest in growth.
\- The 5-year insured warranty differentiated Xicato from competitors with standard 1-year coverage (Programbusiness.com, 2013[29]).
Case study B3: Energy Efficiency Insurance in a hospital facility - United States
Location: United States
Program: HSB Energy Efficiency Insurance
Partners: HSB (Munich Re), Energy Services Company (ESCO)

Background: the hospital facility, originally built in 1970, spans 580 000 square feet. With an annual energy cost baseline of USD 430 000, the hospital recognised the need for significant energy upgrades to reduce costs, enhance operational efficiency and meet sustainability goals. The hospital engaged with an Energy Services Company (ESCO) for an energy efficiency retrofit, which included comprehensive upgrades to the building's infrastructure (Hemic, 2016[30]).
Project description:
\- Technology implemented: the project included 12 energy conservation measures, which were designed to reduce energy usage and improve operational efficiency. These measures included:
HVAC upgrades:
\- Lighting replacements with energy-efficient LEDs
○ Installation of variable frequency drives (VFDs) for motors
\- Water conservation measures (such as low-flow fixtures and systems) (Hemic, 2016[30])
Building type: hospital facility (multi-story, 580 000 sq. ft.)
Total investment (CapEx): USD 2.4 million
Achieved benefits:
\- Annual energy savings: the project was projected to achieve USD 260 000 in annual energy savings.
\- Insured energy savings: HSB's energy efficiency insurance covered 90% of the guaranteed annual energy savings, which amounts to USD 234 000 per year (Hemic, 2016[30]).

\- Insurance coverage: the policy covered shortfalls in annual aggregate efficiency savings as a result of deficiencies in design, implementation and/or performance. Losses were verified via annual measurement and verification reports.
Insurance and loan term: the project was financed with a 10-year loan.

\- Risk mitigation: the energy efficiency insurance covered risks related to the shortfall in energy savings and provided coverage against losses. Additionally, the credit enhancement provided by HSB's solution allowed the ESCO to show significant improvement in the credit rating of the project, which helped reduce the overall cost of the project loan.
\- Financial outcome: With the insurance coverage in place, the hospital was able to reduce financial risks associated with the project, making the large-scale energy improvements more feasible.
Impact:

\- Risk reduction for project stakeholders: the energy efficiency insurance mitigated financial risks, protecting the project owner, contractors and stakeholders from potential performance shortfalls and failures to meet energy savings targets.

\- Improved project financing: the credit enhancement feature helped improve the credit rating of the project, which reduced the overall financing cost and made the investment in energy-saving technologies more financially attractive.

Operational efficiency: with the annual energy savings and improved systems in place, the hospital significantly reduced operational costs while improving energy efficiency across its facility, aligning with sustainability and financial goals.
Case study B4: Performance Insurance for fuel cell technology

Background: in 2013, XL Group's Complex Accounts unit, Munich Re's Green Tech Solutions team, and New Energy Risk (NER) collaborated to offer an innovative performance insurance policy for a portfolio of fuel cell servers installed across the U.S.
Challenge: fuel cell technology manufacturers faced challenges in meeting performance expectations, which could hinder financing and investor confidence.

Solution: The insurance cover provided critical support for project financing by insuring the fuel cells' performance over 15 years, ensuring reliability even if manufacturers couldn't meet warranty obligations. The USD 99 million bond issued to finance the portfolio received an investment-grade rating, enhancing its attractiveness to investors (New Energy Risk, 2014[31]).

Outcome: this collaboration marked the first time that insurance coverage provided by XL Group and Munich Re contributed to a financing bond receiving an investment-grade rating, broadening its appeal to a wider range of investors. The initiative demonstrated the importance of insurance in making clean technology projects more attractive and financially viable (New Energy Risk, 2014[31]).
